questions.question: Guru Har Krishan Ji was which Guru in the line of the ten Sikh Gurus?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Krishan Ji was the eighth Sikh Guru, succeeding his father Guru Har Rai Ji.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru

questions.question: Where was Guru Har Krishan Ji born?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Krishan Ji was born at Kiratpur in the Shivalik foothills, the seat of his father Guru Har Rai Ji.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru

questions.question: Who was the father of Guru Har Krishan Ji?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Krishan Ji was the younger son of Guru Har Rai Ji.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru

questions.question: Guru Har Krishan Ji is remembered as the youngest Guru. At about what age did he become Guru?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Krishan Ji received the Guruship in 1661 when he was about five years old.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru

questions.question: In which year did Guru Har Krishan Ji receive the Guruship?
questions.explanation: He became Guru in 1661, when his father Guru Har Rai Ji passed away at Kiratpur.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru

questions.question: Who complained to Aurangzeb about Guru Har Krishan Ji's succession, leading to the Guru being summoned to Delhi?
questions.explanation: His elder brother Ram Rai, passed over for the Guruship, complained to Aurangzeb, who summoned the young Guru to Delhi.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru

questions.question: In Delhi, Guru Har Krishan Ji stayed as a guest in the residence of which Raja?
options: Mirza Raja Jai Singh of Amber
questions.explanation: Guru Har Krishan Ji stayed at the residence of Mirza Raja Jai Singh of Amber, a Mughal general who conveyed the emperor's summons.
questions.source: ThePrint: Bangla Sahib history

questions.question: Raja Jai Singh's bungalow in Delhi, where Guru Har Krishan Ji stayed, is now which Gurdwara?
questions.explanation: The bungalow became Gurdwara Bangla Sahib; its name likely comes from the word 'bungalow'.
questions.source: ThePrint: Bangla Sahib history

questions.question: Gurdwara Bangla Sahib is located near which well-known area of central Delhi?
questions.explanation: Gurdwara Bangla Sahib stands in central New Delhi, close to Connaught Place.
questions.source: ThePrint: Bangla Sahib history

questions.question: Which epidemic struck Delhi while Guru Har Krishan Ji was there, during which he served the sick?
questions.explanation: Smallpox and cholera broke out in Delhi in 1664; the Guru tended the sick of all faiths and himself caught smallpox.
questions.source: ThePrint: Bangla Sahib history

questions.question: For his service to the sick of all faiths in Delhi, Guru Har Krishan Ji came to be lovingly called what?
questions.explanation: People of all faiths called him 'Bala Pir', the Child Saint, for his compassion during the epidemic.
questions.source: ThePrint: Bangla Sahib history

questions.question: The water of the sarovar at Gurdwara Bangla Sahib is revered by devotees because of its association with what?
options: The Guru's healing of the sick during the epidemic
The compilation of the Adi Granth
questions.explanation: Devotees believe the tank was blessed by Guru Har Krishan Ji and its water healed many during the epidemic; it is revered as amrit.
questions.source: ThePrint: Bangla Sahib history

questions.question: What were Guru Har Krishan Ji's famous last words naming his successor?
questions.explanation: Before passing, he said 'Baba Bakale', meaning the next Guru would be found in the village of Bakala.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru

questions.question: What did Guru Har Krishan Ji's words 'Baba Bakale' indicate?
options: The Sikhs should return to Kiratpur
The Guruship should pass to the scripture
Ram Rai should be the next Guru
The next Guru was an elder ('Baba') at the village of Bakala
questions.explanation: 'Baba Bakale' meant the successor was a 'Baba' (elder) at Bakala; this proved to be Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, his grand-uncle.
questions.source: Sikhs.org: Guru Tegh Bahadur

questions.question: Who turned out to be the 'Baba' at Bakala named by Guru Har Krishan Ji as successor?
questions.explanation: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, meditating at Bakala, was revealed as the ninth Guru.
questions.source: Sikhs.org: Guru Tegh Bahadur

questions.question: In which year did Guru Har Krishan Ji pass away in Delhi?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Krishan Ji passed away in Delhi in 1664 after contracting smallpox while serving the sick.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru

questions.question: Where was Guru Har Krishan Ji cremated, on the then bank of the Yamuna?
questions.explanation: He was cremated on the bank of the Yamuna at the site of Gurdwara Bala Sahib, New Delhi.
questions.source: All About Sikhs: Gurudwara Bala Sahib, New Delhi

questions.question: Besides Guru Har Krishan Ji's cremation, Gurdwara Bala Sahib also marks the cremation of which two revered women?
options: Mata Sundri and Mata Sahib Kaur
questions.explanation: Mata Sundri and Mata Sahib Kaur were also cremated at the Bala Sahib site.
questions.source: All About Sikhs: Gurudwara Bala Sahib, New Delhi

questions.question: On the way to Delhi at Panjokhra, who explained the Bhagavad Gita to humble a proud pandit, by the Guru's grace?
questions.explanation: At Panjokhra, the Guru's grace enabled the unlettered water-carrier Chhajju Ram to expound the Gita, humbling the pandit.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru

questions.question: What was the name of the learned pandit at Panjokhra who challenged Guru Har Krishan Ji?
questions.explanation: Pandit Lal Chand challenged the young Guru; after Chhajju's exposition of the Gita, he became a disciple.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Krishan, Guru
